turn1.explanation: The unit responds mainly to the faces of small to medium furry mammals seen from the front, such as cats, foxes, red pandas, hamsters, meerkats and ferrets, with the eyes, snout and fur texture prominent. It shows a weaker spillover to other subjects, as in the red car.
turn1.evidence: 19 of the top 20 images are furry mammals, mostly cats and foxes, and nearly all show a frontal face with visible eyes and fur (fox at 10, cats at 9, red panda at 9). The one exception is the red Mercedes convertible at 9, whose rounded front with its headlights may resemble a face, or which may be a genuinely separate trigger.
turn1.missing_data: Lower-ranked and near-zero activations would show whether dogs, larger mammals, faceless fur textures, or other face-like objects such as car fronts also drive the unit. That would separate a face-shape explanation from a fur-texture explanation and test whether the car is a real second trigger.
